name: VaultFeed
author: CCGnomes

sections.description:
VaultFeed displays social media feeds on your WordPress site while keeping your OAuth tokens encrypted on your own server — never uploaded to a third-party SaaS platform.

Connect accounts from these feed sources: Facebook, Instagram, Twitter / X, YouTube, TikTok, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Mastodon, Reddit, Snapchat, Twitch, Vimeo, Google Business Profile, Yelp, and more. Every token is AES-256-GCM encrypted and stored only in your own database.

Features

VaultFeed is fully functional with no artificial limits on feed count, post count, or layout — everything below is included with the plugin as distributed on WordPress.org:

  • Connect accounts from these feed sources: Facebook Pages, Instagram Business / Creator, Twitter / X, YouTube, TikTok, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Mastodon (public accounts, no credentials needed), Reddit, Snapchat (Snap Kit Display API), Twitch (clips and VODs via Helix API), Vimeo (user/channel/group feeds), Google Business Profile, Yelp, and more
  • Display photo, video, reel, and review feeds in Grid, List, Masonry, Highlight, Waterfall, Stories, Carousel, Slider, Ticker, Timeline, or Wall layout (11 in all)
  • Star-rating widget with WCAG-compliant aria-label for review feeds
  • Configurable columns (1–6), aspect ratio, hover effects, and post count
  • Lightbox for photos and videos with keyboard navigation
  • Load More button and infinite scroll
  • Feed header with optional follow button
  • Shortcode [vaultfeed id="N"] and Gutenberg block
  • Automatic content caching with configurable TTL, fully adjustable
  • Caption display, source icon, date, and like / comment counts
  • Optional “Powered by VaultFeed” attribution link — off by default, opt-in only
  • Fully translatable — .pot file included
  • WCAG 2.1 AA compliant — focus traps, live regions, 4.5:1 contrast
  • Zero telemetry — nothing phones home

Pro add-on

A separately sold Pro add-on is planned and will be available from the VaultFeed website. It will not be distributed via WordPress.org, and none of its code is included in this plugin. It will add functionality that depends on infrastructure this plugin does not include or run:

  • ReelVault source — a video feed served from your own self-hosted Holochain node (requires running that node yourself; VaultFeed does not bundle or install it)
  • DHT token storage as an alternative to the local database storage described below
  • Priority support

None of this is locked or hidden in the WordPress.org version; it is simply not part of this plugin.

How token storage works

When you connect an account, VaultFeed encrypts the OAuth token with AES-256-GCM and stores it in your own WordPress database. The encryption key is derived from your WordPress secret keys and a random per-installation salt that is generated at first activation and stored in your WordPress database (the vaultfeed_token_salt option). VaultFeed never writes to wp-config.php or to any WordPress core, plugin, or theme file. No token ever leaves your server.

External services

VaultFeed relies on third-party services to do its job: it fetches feed content from the social platforms you explicitly connect, and it can optionally send data to a small number of integrations (email marketing, analytics, notifications, store lookups, AI caption rewriting) that stay completely inactive until you enter your own credentials or URL for them. Every service the plugin can contact is listed below with what is sent, when, and its terms and privacy policy. No data is ever sent to VaultFeed or its authors; the plugin operates no background service and has no telemetry.

  1. Facebook Graph API (graph.facebook.com) — when you initiate an OAuth connection from the Accounts page, and when fetching feed content. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Facebook account.

  2. Instagram Graph API (graph.instagram.com, graph.facebook.com) — when you initiate an Instagram OAuth connection from the Accounts page, and when fetching Instagram feed, tagged-post, or story content. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Instagram’s Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Instagram account.

  3. Twitter / X API v2 (api.twitter.com) — when you initiate a Twitter OAuth 2.0 PKCE connection, and when fetching tweet content. Governed by X’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Twitter account.

  4. Google / YouTube Data API v3 (accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, www.googleapis.com) — when you initiate a Google OAuth 2.0 connection (your browser is sent to Google’s consent screen), and when fetching YouTube channel or playlist content. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected YouTube account.

  5. TikTok for Developers API v2 (www.tiktok.com, open.tiktokapis.com) — when you initiate a TikTok OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching video content. Governed by TikTok’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected TikTok account.

  6. Threads API (graph.threads.net) — when you initiate a Threads OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching posts. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Threads account.

  7. Google Business Profile APIs (mybusiness.googleapis.com, mybusinessaccountmanagement.googleapis.com, mybusinessbusinessinformation.googleapis.com) — when listing your business accounts/locations and when fetching Google business reviews. Uses the same Google OAuth credentials as YouTube (item 4 above); both APIs must be enabled in your Google Cloud project. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Google Business Profile account.

  8. Yelp Fusion API (api.yelp.com) — when you verify a Yelp API key connection, and when fetching business reviews. Governed by Yelp’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Yelp account.

  9. LinkedIn REST API (api.linkedin.com) — when you initiate a LinkedIn OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching posts. Governed by LinkedIn’s User Agreement and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected LinkedIn account.

  10. Bluesky AT Protocol API (bsky.social, public.api.bsky.app) — when you connect a Bluesky account via App Password, and when fetching posts. Governed by Bluesky’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Bluesky account.

  11. Pinterest API (api.pinterest.com) — when you initiate a Pinterest OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching boards and pins. Governed by Pinterest’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Pinterest account.

  12. Mastodon API ({your-instance}/api/v1/) — when you look up a Mastodon account by handle, and when fetching public statuses. The specific domain depends on the Mastodon instance you connect, and each instance publishes its own terms and privacy policy — for example, mastodon.social’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Mastodon account.

  13. Reddit OAuth2 / REST API (oauth.reddit.com, www.reddit.com) — when you initiate a Reddit OAuth 2.0 client-credentials connection, and when fetching subreddit posts. Governed by Reddit’s User Agreement and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Reddit account.

  14. Snapchat Login Kit / Snap Kit Display API (accounts.snapchat.com, kit.snapchat.com) — when you initiate a Snapchat OAuth 2.0 connection and exchange or refresh its token, and when fetching your profile and public stories. Governed by Snapchat’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Snapchat account.

  15. Twitch Helix API (id.twitch.tv, api.twitch.tv) — when you connect a Twitch app (an app access token is requested from id.twitch.tv), and when fetching clips and VODs. Governed by Twitch’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Twitch account.

  16. Vimeo API (api.vimeo.com) — when you connect a Vimeo account via Personal Access Token, and when fetching user, channel, or group video feeds. Governed by Vimeo’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Vimeo account.

  17. AI caption rewriting — via the WordPress AI Client — optional, and never automatic: it runs only when you click “Enhance Caption” on the Moderation screen, and sends only that one caption’s text plus a short rewrite instruction (the chosen tone). No OAuth tokens, visitor data, or other site data is ever included. VaultFeed hands the request to WordPress’s built-in AI Client (WordPress 7.0 and later), so the text goes to whichever AI provider you have connected under WordPress’s own AI settings; VaultFeed stores no credentials for it and contacts no AI provider on its own, and that provider’s terms and privacy policy apply. If you have not connected an AI provider in WordPress, the feature is simply unavailable and nothing is sent anywhere.

  18. Mailchimp Marketing API (<dc>.api.mailchimp.com) — used only by the optional email-capture feature. Only active if you enable email capture on a feed and enter your own Mailchimp API key and Audience (list) ID in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor submits the email-capture form, their email address is sent to Mailchimp to be added as a subscriber to your audience. Nothing is sent if a Mailchimp key is not configured. Governed by Mailchimp’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

  19. ConvertKit / Kit API (api.convertkit.com) — used only by the optional email-capture feature. Only active if you enable email capture on a feed and enter your own ConvertKit (Kit) API key and Form ID in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor submits the email-capture form, their email address is sent to ConvertKit to subscribe them to your form. Nothing is sent if a ConvertKit key is not configured. Governed by Kit’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  20. Google Analytics 4 Measurement Protocol (www.google-analytics.com) — used only for optional click analytics. Only active if you enter your own GA4 Measurement ID and API Secret in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor clicks a post, a vaultfeed_click event (feed ID, post ID, and post type — no personal data) is sent to your Google Analytics property. Nothing is sent if GA4 credentials are not configured. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  21. Slack incoming webhooks (hooks.slack.com) — used only for optional new-post notifications. Only active if you paste your own Slack incoming-webhook URL in VaultFeed → Settings and enable new-post alerts on a feed. When new posts arrive in that feed, a short text message (the number of new posts and the feed’s name — no post content and no visitor data) is sent to your Slack webhook. Nothing is sent if no Slack URL is configured. Governed by Slack’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  22. Zapier webhooks (hooks.zapier.com) — used only for optional automation. Only active if you paste your own Zapier “Catch Hook” URL in VaultFeed → Settings. When a feed refresh finds new posts, the feed ID and, for each new post, its platform ID, caption text, first media URL, permalink, and timestamp are sent to your Zapier webhook. This is public social content you chose to display — no visitor data is included. Nothing is sent if no Zapier URL is configured. Governed by Zapier’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  23. Shopify Storefront API ({your-store}.myshopify.com) — used only by the optional “Shop” badge. Only active if you enter your own Shopify store URL and Storefront API access token in VaultFeed → Settings and enable the shop badge on a feed. When a post’s hashtag has no product link you mapped manually, that hashtag is sent to your own store’s Storefront API as a product-handle lookup, together with your Storefront token, to find the product’s URL (results are cached for one hour). No visitor data is sent. Nothing is sent if Shopify is not configured. Governed by Shopify’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  24. Your own outbound webhook URLs — optional. Only active if you add one or more webhook endpoints in VaultFeed → Webhooks. When an event you selected fires (feed refreshed, feed error, post approved/rejected), a JSON payload is POSTed to the URL(s) you entered: the event name, the feed ID, and for refresh events each post’s platform ID, type, source, caption text (first 280 characters), permalink, and publish date. Requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using your webhook secret. The destination is whatever server you specify, so its terms and privacy policy are those of the service you choose; no data goes anywhere unless you add a URL.

  25. Social platform media CDNs (for example scontent.cdninstagram.com, pbs.twimg.com, i.ytimg.com — the exact hosts depend on the platforms you connect) — the images, thumbnails and videos inside your feeds are served from the platform’s own CDN, so a visitor’s browser requests them directly from that platform while viewing the feed, exactly as an ordinary embedded post would. The URLs come from the platform API response; VaultFeed does not rehost them. The platform’s terms and privacy policy are the ones listed for that platform above. If you would rather your visitors never contact those CDNs, switch on the built-in image proxy — wp option update vaultfeed_image_proxy_enabled 1 — and your own server fetches and caches the images instead.

  26. YouTube embedded player (www.youtube-nocookie.com) — only when a visitor clicks a YouTube video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads YouTube’s player directly, so YouTube receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. YouTube Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

  27. Vimeo embedded player (player.vimeo.com) — only when a visitor clicks a Vimeo video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads Vimeo’s player directly, so Vimeo receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. Vimeo Terms, Vimeo Privacy Policy.

  28. TikTok embedded player (www.tiktok.com) — only when a visitor clicks a TikTok video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads TikTok’s player directly, so TikTok receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. TikTok Terms, TikTok Privacy Policy.

  29. Twitch embedded player (player.twitch.tv for videos, clips.twitch.tv for clips) — only when a visitor clicks a Twitch video or clip; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads Twitch’s player directly, so Twitch receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address (your site’s host name is passed as the parent setting Twitch requires) and the video or clip ID, and may set cookies. Twitch Terms, Twitch Privacy Policy.

  30. WordPress.org update API — standard WordPress plugin update check behaviour. No VaultFeed-specific data is transmitted beyond the plugin slug and current version.

Third-party libraries

VaultFeed’s own scripts, styles and fonts are all bundled with the plugin — none are loaded from an external server or CDN. (The post images and videos inside your feeds are a separate matter: those are served from the social platforms’ CDNs, as described in item 25 of “External services” above.)

  • SortableJS 1.15.7 (MIT licence) — drag-to-reorder on the admin Moderation screen. Bundled at assets/js/vendor/sortable.min.js with the unminified source alongside at assets/js/vendor/sortable.js and the upstream licence at assets/js/vendor/sortable-LICENSE.txt. Source: github.com/SortableJS/Sortable.
  • All other minified files in assets/js/*.min.js and assets/css/*.min.css are built from the human-readable .js / .css files of the same name that ship next to them.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the vaultfeed folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin via Plugins → Installed Plugins
  3. Go to VaultFeed → Settings and enter your app credentials for the platforms you want to use
  4. Go to VaultFeed → Accounts and connect your accounts
  5. Go to VaultFeed → Feeds and click + New Feed to create your first feed
  6. Copy the shortcode (e.g. [vaultfeed id="1"]) and paste it into any post, page, or widget

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.4 or later
  • PHP 8.1 or later
  • Developer credentials for each platform you wish to connect:
    • Facebook / Instagram — a Meta Developer App with pages_read_engagement and instagram_basic permissions
    • Twitter / X — a Twitter Developer App with OAuth 2.0 enabled and scopes tweet.read users.read offline.access
    • YouTube — Google Cloud OAuth 2.0 credentials with the YouTube Data API v3 enabled
    • TikTok — a TikTok Developer App with user.info.basic and video.list scopes
    • Threads — a Meta Developer App with threads_basic permissions (separate from your Facebook / Instagram app)
    • Google Business Profile reviews — same Google Cloud project as YouTube, with the Business Profile APIs additionally enabled
    • Yelp — a Yelp Fusion API key from the Yelp developer portal
    • LinkedIn — a LinkedIn Developer App with openid profile email r_member_social w_member_social scopes enabled
    • Bluesky — no developer account needed; create an App Password at bsky.app → Settings → App Passwords
    • Pinterest — a Pinterest Developer App with boards:read, pins:read, and user_accounts:read scopes
    • Mastodon — no credentials required; public accounts are accessible via the Mastodon public API
sections.faq:
Do I need developer accounts for the platforms I want to connect?

Most platforms require their own developer app credentials, entered in VaultFeed → Settings. The setup takes 10–15 minutes per platform. Two exceptions: Bluesky uses an App Password (no developer account needed), and Mastodon uses public accounts with no credentials at all. The credentials each platform needs are listed under Installation → Requirements above, and each platform’s section in VaultFeed → Settings links to the matching developer portal. For the exact OAuth callback URL and required scopes for each platform, plus troubleshooting, see the VaultFeed setup guide.

Where can I get help?

Setup, troubleshooting, and a support ticket form are on the VaultFeed Setup & Support page. You can also use the plugin’s support forum here on WordPress.org.

Where are my OAuth tokens stored?

Tokens are stored in the vaultfeed_tokens table in your WordPress database, encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The encryption key is derived locally from your AUTH_KEY and a random salt stored in your WordPress database (VaultFeed does not write to wp-config.php). No token is ever transmitted to VaultFeed or any third party.

Is there a limit on feeds, posts, or layouts in the free version?

No. There is no cap on the number of feeds you can create, no cap on posts per feed, and all eleven layouts (Grid, List, Masonry, Highlight, Waterfall, Stories, Carousel, Slider, Ticker, Timeline, Wall) are available. The optional “Powered by VaultFeed” attribution link is off by default and only appears if you turn it on yourself in a feed’s Display Settings.

Does this work with WordPress multisite?

Yes. Each sub-site manages its feeds and account connections independently.

Is this GDPR-compliant?

VaultFeed sends nothing to its authors and makes no unsolicited third-party network calls. By default it stores no visitor personal data: click and impression analytics are aggregate counters, and the visitor IP address is used only transiently (hashed, in short-lived rate-limit/de-duplication keys) and is never stored in readable form. If you turn on the optional email capture form, the addresses visitors submit are sent to the Mailchimp or ConvertKit account you configured — or, if neither is configured, kept in your own WordPress database — so you are the data controller for them and should disclose that in your Privacy Policy. Your wider GDPR obligations depend on the content of your social media feeds and your agreements with the respective platforms. See the “External services” section for exactly what each optional integration sends.

Can I display the same feed on multiple pages?

Yes — use the same shortcode [vaultfeed id="N"] anywhere on your site. The cached content is shared so it counts as one API call.

Does the plugin support Instagram Stories?

Yes (free tier). Stories are a feed type you can choose in the feed creation wizard, step 3.

Is my data sent to VaultFeed servers?

No. VaultFeed operates no background service and receives no data from your site. Out of the box, the plugin makes outbound HTTP calls only to the social platforms you explicitly connect (to fetch feed content) and to the WordPress.org API (to check for plugin updates). The optional integrations listed under “External services” (Mailchimp, ConvertKit, Google Analytics 4, Slack, Zapier, Shopify, and your own webhooks) contact those services only after you enter your own credentials or URL for them — and even then, the data goes to your account with that service, never to VaultFeed. Your OAuth tokens never leave your server.

Does this work with caching plugins?

Yes. VaultFeed maintains its own server-side cache in the vaultfeed_feed_cache database table, independent of any full-page cache. Feeds load correctly behind WP Super Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, and similar plugins. If you use a page cache with a very long TTL, enable auto-refresh in your feed’s Display Settings so content stays current without a full page reload.

What PHP version is required?

PHP 8.1 or higher is required. PHP 8.2 and 8.3 are fully supported. WordPress 6.4 or higher is required.

My theme is always dark and an Auto feed is hard to read. What do I do?

A feed whose Dark Mode setting is Auto follows the visitor’s browser, not the theme. On a theme that is dark whatever the browser says, set the feed’s Dark Mode to Dark (or Light, for a light panel of its own).

What happens if my token expires?

Most platforms issue short-lived access tokens (X, YouTube, TikTok and Google, for example), and VaultFeed renews them by itself before a fetch. Facebook, Instagram and Threads tokens are renewed before they run out. An account is marked “Expiring soon” on the Accounts page, with a notice in the WordPress admin and an e-mail (unless you turned it off in Settings), only when it cannot renew itself. That happens when the platform refused a renewal or rejected the account (for example, access was revoked), when its token is about to end and cannot be renewed, or when it ran out and could not be renewed for a day. A passing error (a timeout, the platform down for a moment) is only retried. Click Reconnect on the account card. Until you do, its feeds cannot fetch new posts.
sections.changelog:
0.9.4

Fixes found on clean installs and on a live X feed. No database schema changes; the update corrects the reconnect dates stored for X, TikTok, Google reviews, Snapchat, LinkedIn, Pinterest and Threads accounts.

  • Fix: captions and other text were unreadable in a dark browser (Card, Clean, Bubble, every colour preset, the Wall layout) and in a feed set to Dark; every text now has enough contrast in light and dark, and a feed set to Light stays light.
  • Fix: Settings > Theme Colors undid dark mode once the Settings page had been saved (dark text on a dark card). Colours left at their defaults are no longer stored, and a colour you chose applies to the light palette only.
  • Fix: the classic VaultFeed widget never appeared in Appearance > Widgets; it does now.
  • Fix: right-to-left sites loaded no feed stylesheet.
  • Fix: a default of “Pagination: None” in Settings was lost when creating a feed; the wizard offers None.
  • Fix: deactivating or deleting the plugin left per-feed refresh events in WP-Cron.
  • Fix: the widget’s posts-per-page setting is held to 1-50 like the shortcode and block.
  • Fix: the shortcode, the block, the widget and the Settings page accepted only six of the eleven layouts, so layout=”highlight” (or Stories, Ticker, Timeline, Wall) was ignored; they now accept all eleven.
  • Fix: the feed wizard showed its display settings on every step; each step now shows on its own.
  • Fix: the Feed saved! step shows the iFrame embed code instead of an empty box.
  • Fix: the live preview no longer sits on “Loading preview…”; it answers or says it is taking too long.
  • Fix: the preview’s Tablet and Mobile buttons apply the feed’s tablet and phone column settings.
  • Fix: all ten post styles save (Modern, Magazine, Bubble, Compact and Story were silently dropped), and every menu that offers a post style lists all ten.
  • Fix: the readme listed nine layouts; there are eleven.
  • Fix: a visitor’s choice on a feed’s dark-mode toggle changed every feed set to Dark or Light on the site; it now applies to Toggle feeds only. In a dark browser the toggle’s first click now turns the feed light, and its pressed state is right from the start.
  • Fix: on right-to-left sites the feed header, post details, share buttons and post window ran left to right; the iFrame embed page is right-to-left too.
  • Fix: a feed set to refresh every hour (the wizard’s default) refreshed at its source’s own interval instead: every 15 minutes on X, four times the X API reads. A feed now refreshes at the interval it shows. The wizard also offers the source’s own interval by name, and leaves out intervals shorter than the source allows.
  • Fix: X accounts (and TikTok, Google reviews and Snapchat accounts) showed “Expiring soon” and asked to be reconnected straight after connecting, and the expiry e-mail was sent, although they renew themselves; LinkedIn, Pinterest and Threads accounts never warned before their access ended. An account now asks for a reconnect only when it cannot renew itself, the platform refused a renewal, or renewing has failed for a day. The update corrects the stored dates of X, TikTok, Google reviews, Snapchat, LinkedIn, Pinterest and Threads accounts.
  • Fix: a revoked connection asks for a reconnect on every source that signs in except Twitch (Mastodon and the site’s own posts have nothing to revoke), not only YouTube. When a platform calls an access token invalid on a fetch, VaultFeed renews it at once and asks for a reconnect if the renewal is refused.
  • Fix: an X mentions feed stopped loading two hours after connecting (its X token was never renewed).
  • Fix: Facebook, Instagram and Threads tokens are renewed before they run out.
  • Fix: a feed first loaded by a page view now shows when it was synced.
  • Fix: X posts with a video or GIF showed as text only; they show their picture with a play button and play in the lightbox. Instagram, Instagram tagged and Threads videos are fixed the same way.
  • Fix: X posts showed raw t.co links. The link to the post’s own media is removed, and every other link shows readably; in a caption under a picture (every style but Overlap) it opens the real address, and the RSS feed, the JSON Feed, webhooks and the REST API carry the real address. Bluesky and Mastodon links are handled the same way.
  • Fix: the feed wizard’s preview fetched from the platform on every change (each one cost X reads). It uses the feed’s cache or one fetch, kept for the feed’s refresh interval, or for ten minutes when it found no posts (fetched again once the account is reconnected).
  • Fix: a platform’s rate limit or quota now pauses the feed on every source: until the platform’s reset time when it gives one, otherwise for a fixed pause (before, most sources were called again every few minutes).
  • Fix: a failed sync shows the platform’s own reason on every source, and a failed sign-in on every source that signs in with OAuth (X, TikTok, Google reviews, Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, Threads, LinkedIn and Pinterest), not only YouTube.
  • Fix: the feed wizard offers the Dark mode setting.
  • Fix: a post without a picture (a text-only X post, for example) showed its text twice, without padding, with a lighter strip below it. It now shows once, in its card, padded.
  • New: a feed’s Text-only posts setting shows such a post’s full text, or shortens it to five lines with a Show more / Show less button that opens the rest in place (the default; a feed whose captions show in full shows the full text).
  • Fix: in a classic theme’s sidebar (Twenty Twenty-One) post text, the ticker, the Follow button and typed text took the theme’s link colour and were unreadable.
  • Fix: the dark-mode toggle covered the Follow button; the Overlap style laid its caption over the share buttons and, on posts without a picture, over the post’s own text; the Wall layout’s source label and the carousel arrows covered post text.
  • Fix: in the Overlap style a long caption was cut through the middle of a line, was hard to read over a light picture and, in narrow cards or with a long author name, ran under the meta badge or the call to action or disappeared; it now ends on a whole line with an ellipsis on a darker backing and keeps clear of both, and a meta badge with no room on the picture moves under it. Its “Show more” button, which could not be reached on the picture, is gone there (the post window shows the whole caption). A call to action wider than a narrow card was cut off; it now wraps inside the picture. In the Stories layout the call to action was drawn as a tall 9:16 box.
  • Fix: a long word or web address in a caption ran past the card’s edge in every post style; it now wraps.
  • Fix: a Ticker feed in a narrow widget area (Twenty Twenty-One’s footer) or in a Row block widened the page by thousands of pixels.
  • Fix: date, likes and other grey text reached only 4.33:1 on a tinted page; a feed set to Light now has a light panel of its own in any browser.
  • Fix: deleting the plugin left its widgets listed in the theme’s widget areas.
  • Fix: search and the source tabs left posts on screen in the List, Masonry and Waterfall layouts (and posts without a picture in the others), and never filtered a Wall or Ticker feed; they work in every layout now.
  • Fix: with the same feed twice on a page, the second copy’s Load more filled the first; each copy loads into itself, and no id repeats on a page. The e-mail sign-up field has a label, and the feed’s messages for screen readers are translated.

0.9.3

One fix. No database changes.

  • Fix: feeds on quiet pages now refresh on schedule; the stale-feed email is sent once per problem and says why.

0.9.2

Two display fixes. No database changes.

  • Fix: a feed’s Custom CSS now reaches the page (it was dropped on block themes).
  • Fix: the highlight layout’s hero image fills the full width of the feed instead of leaving an empty strip on wide pages.

0.9.1

Fixes found on a live YouTube feed. Adds a small data migration (YouTube reconnect date only).

  • Fix: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and Twitch videos play in the lightbox and the post window using each platform’s official embedded player; Bluesky videos play where the browser supports them natively.
  • Fix: closing the lightbox or post window stops the video.
  • Fix: a freshly connected YouTube account no longer shows “Expiring soon”; every account whose access token expires is renewed before a feed is fetched.
  • Fix: a failed refresh no longer replaces good cached posts with an empty list; the feed list and Analytics show why a sync failed.
  • Fix: the hashtag shortcode keeps showing the last cached posts when its cache has just expired.
  • Fix: a refresh that returned posts was recorded as failed whenever the Zapier listener ran.

0.9.0

Fixes found by independent audits. No database changes.

  • Security (WP.org review): the feed-import upload reader no longer carries any phpcs:ignore for a sanitisation rule and no longer alters PHP’s temporary file path.
  • Fix: the wizard’s live preview, editing of aggregated feeds, and the legacy widget and block editor now keep feeds that are paused, scheduled or in error instead of dropping them.
  • Security: the block editor lists non-active feeds only to users who can edit others’ posts; an aggregated feed’s RSS ETag and Last-Modified respect each reader’s visibility.
  • Fix: stored schedules without a time zone are shown as the UTC instant the server enforces.

0.8.9

Supersedes the unreleased 0.8.6, 0.8.7 and 0.8.8 builds. Many security and correctness fixes: feed visibility is enforced on every REST, RSS, shortcode and embed surface, and editing a feed in the wizard no longer resets fields the form did not change.

0.8.5 and earlier

Plugin Check and WP.org review fixes, and security hardening of the public endpoints.

Full history: see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

short_description: Self-sovereign social feeds: your tokens stay encrypted on your own server, never uploaded to a third party.
description:
VaultFeed displays social media feeds on your WordPress site while keeping your OAuth tokens encrypted on your own server — never uploaded to a third-party SaaS platform.

Connect accounts from these feed sources: Facebook, Instagram, Twitter / X, YouTube, TikTok, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Mastodon, Reddit, Snapchat, Twitch, Vimeo, Google Business Profile, Yelp, and more. Every token is AES-256-GCM encrypted and stored only in your own database.

Features

VaultFeed is fully functional with no artificial limits on feed count, post count, or layout — everything below is included with the plugin as distributed on WordPress.org:

  • Connect accounts from these feed sources: Facebook Pages, Instagram Business / Creator, Twitter / X, YouTube, TikTok, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Pinterest, Mastodon (public accounts, no credentials needed), Reddit, Snapchat (Snap Kit Display API), Twitch (clips and VODs via Helix API), Vimeo (user/channel/group feeds), Google Business Profile, Yelp, and more
  • Display photo, video, reel, and review feeds in Grid, List, Masonry, Highlight, Waterfall, Stories, Carousel, Slider, Ticker, Timeline, or Wall layout (11 in all)
  • Star-rating widget with WCAG-compliant aria-label for review feeds
  • Configurable columns (1–6), aspect ratio, hover effects, and post count
  • Lightbox for photos and videos with keyboard navigation
  • Load More button and infinite scroll
  • Feed header with optional follow button
  • Shortcode [vaultfeed id="N"] and Gutenberg block
  • Automatic content caching with configurable TTL, fully adjustable
  • Caption display, source icon, date, and like / comment counts
  • Optional “Powered by VaultFeed” attribution link — off by default, opt-in only
  • Fully translatable — .pot file included
  • WCAG 2.1 AA compliant — focus traps, live regions, 4.5:1 contrast
  • Zero telemetry — nothing phones home

Pro add-on

A separately sold Pro add-on is planned and will be available from the VaultFeed website. It will not be distributed via WordPress.org, and none of its code is included in this plugin. It will add functionality that depends on infrastructure this plugin does not include or run:

  • ReelVault source — a video feed served from your own self-hosted Holochain node (requires running that node yourself; VaultFeed does not bundle or install it)
  • DHT token storage as an alternative to the local database storage described below
  • Priority support

None of this is locked or hidden in the WordPress.org version; it is simply not part of this plugin.

How token storage works

When you connect an account, VaultFeed encrypts the OAuth token with AES-256-GCM and stores it in your own WordPress database. The encryption key is derived from your WordPress secret keys and a random per-installation salt that is generated at first activation and stored in your WordPress database (the vaultfeed_token_salt option). VaultFeed never writes to wp-config.php or to any WordPress core, plugin, or theme file. No token ever leaves your server.

External services

VaultFeed relies on third-party services to do its job: it fetches feed content from the social platforms you explicitly connect, and it can optionally send data to a small number of integrations (email marketing, analytics, notifications, store lookups, AI caption rewriting) that stay completely inactive until you enter your own credentials or URL for them. Every service the plugin can contact is listed below with what is sent, when, and its terms and privacy policy. No data is ever sent to VaultFeed or its authors; the plugin operates no background service and has no telemetry.

  1. Facebook Graph API (graph.facebook.com) — when you initiate an OAuth connection from the Accounts page, and when fetching feed content. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Facebook account.

  2. Instagram Graph API (graph.instagram.com, graph.facebook.com) — when you initiate an Instagram OAuth connection from the Accounts page, and when fetching Instagram feed, tagged-post, or story content. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Instagram’s Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Instagram account.

  3. Twitter / X API v2 (api.twitter.com) — when you initiate a Twitter OAuth 2.0 PKCE connection, and when fetching tweet content. Governed by X’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Twitter account.

  4. Google / YouTube Data API v3 (accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, www.googleapis.com) — when you initiate a Google OAuth 2.0 connection (your browser is sent to Google’s consent screen), and when fetching YouTube channel or playlist content. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected YouTube account.

  5. TikTok for Developers API v2 (www.tiktok.com, open.tiktokapis.com) — when you initiate a TikTok OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching video content. Governed by TikTok’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected TikTok account.

  6. Threads API (graph.threads.net) — when you initiate a Threads OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching posts. Governed by Meta’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Threads account.

  7. Google Business Profile APIs (mybusiness.googleapis.com, mybusinessaccountmanagement.googleapis.com, mybusinessbusinessinformation.googleapis.com) — when listing your business accounts/locations and when fetching Google business reviews. Uses the same Google OAuth credentials as YouTube (item 4 above); both APIs must be enabled in your Google Cloud project. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Google Business Profile account.

  8. Yelp Fusion API (api.yelp.com) — when you verify a Yelp API key connection, and when fetching business reviews. Governed by Yelp’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Yelp account.

  9. LinkedIn REST API (api.linkedin.com) — when you initiate a LinkedIn OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching posts. Governed by LinkedIn’s User Agreement and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected LinkedIn account.

  10. Bluesky AT Protocol API (bsky.social, public.api.bsky.app) — when you connect a Bluesky account via App Password, and when fetching posts. Governed by Bluesky’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Bluesky account.

  11. Pinterest API (api.pinterest.com) — when you initiate a Pinterest OAuth 2.0 connection, and when fetching boards and pins. Governed by Pinterest’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Pinterest account.

  12. Mastodon API ({your-instance}/api/v1/) — when you look up a Mastodon account by handle, and when fetching public statuses. The specific domain depends on the Mastodon instance you connect, and each instance publishes its own terms and privacy policy — for example, mastodon.social’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Mastodon account.

  13. Reddit OAuth2 / REST API (oauth.reddit.com, www.reddit.com) — when you initiate a Reddit OAuth 2.0 client-credentials connection, and when fetching subreddit posts. Governed by Reddit’s User Agreement and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Reddit account.

  14. Snapchat Login Kit / Snap Kit Display API (accounts.snapchat.com, kit.snapchat.com) — when you initiate a Snapchat OAuth 2.0 connection and exchange or refresh its token, and when fetching your profile and public stories. Governed by Snapchat’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Snapchat account.

  15. Twitch Helix API (id.twitch.tv, api.twitch.tv) — when you connect a Twitch app (an app access token is requested from id.twitch.tv), and when fetching clips and VODs. Governed by Twitch’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Twitch account.

  16. Vimeo API (api.vimeo.com) — when you connect a Vimeo account via Personal Access Token, and when fetching user, channel, or group video feeds. Governed by Vimeo’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy. Only called when you have a connected Vimeo account.

  17. AI caption rewriting — via the WordPress AI Client — optional, and never automatic: it runs only when you click “Enhance Caption” on the Moderation screen, and sends only that one caption’s text plus a short rewrite instruction (the chosen tone). No OAuth tokens, visitor data, or other site data is ever included. VaultFeed hands the request to WordPress’s built-in AI Client (WordPress 7.0 and later), so the text goes to whichever AI provider you have connected under WordPress’s own AI settings; VaultFeed stores no credentials for it and contacts no AI provider on its own, and that provider’s terms and privacy policy apply. If you have not connected an AI provider in WordPress, the feature is simply unavailable and nothing is sent anywhere.

  18. Mailchimp Marketing API (<dc>.api.mailchimp.com) — used only by the optional email-capture feature. Only active if you enable email capture on a feed and enter your own Mailchimp API key and Audience (list) ID in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor submits the email-capture form, their email address is sent to Mailchimp to be added as a subscriber to your audience. Nothing is sent if a Mailchimp key is not configured. Governed by Mailchimp’s Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

  19. ConvertKit / Kit API (api.convertkit.com) — used only by the optional email-capture feature. Only active if you enable email capture on a feed and enter your own ConvertKit (Kit) API key and Form ID in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor submits the email-capture form, their email address is sent to ConvertKit to subscribe them to your form. Nothing is sent if a ConvertKit key is not configured. Governed by Kit’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  20. Google Analytics 4 Measurement Protocol (www.google-analytics.com) — used only for optional click analytics. Only active if you enter your own GA4 Measurement ID and API Secret in VaultFeed → Settings. When a visitor clicks a post, a vaultfeed_click event (feed ID, post ID, and post type — no personal data) is sent to your Google Analytics property. Nothing is sent if GA4 credentials are not configured. Governed by Google’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  21. Slack incoming webhooks (hooks.slack.com) — used only for optional new-post notifications. Only active if you paste your own Slack incoming-webhook URL in VaultFeed → Settings and enable new-post alerts on a feed. When new posts arrive in that feed, a short text message (the number of new posts and the feed’s name — no post content and no visitor data) is sent to your Slack webhook. Nothing is sent if no Slack URL is configured. Governed by Slack’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  22. Zapier webhooks (hooks.zapier.com) — used only for optional automation. Only active if you paste your own Zapier “Catch Hook” URL in VaultFeed → Settings. When a feed refresh finds new posts, the feed ID and, for each new post, its platform ID, caption text, first media URL, permalink, and timestamp are sent to your Zapier webhook. This is public social content you chose to display — no visitor data is included. Nothing is sent if no Zapier URL is configured. Governed by Zapier’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  23. Shopify Storefront API ({your-store}.myshopify.com) — used only by the optional “Shop” badge. Only active if you enter your own Shopify store URL and Storefront API access token in VaultFeed → Settings and enable the shop badge on a feed. When a post’s hashtag has no product link you mapped manually, that hashtag is sent to your own store’s Storefront API as a product-handle lookup, together with your Storefront token, to find the product’s URL (results are cached for one hour). No visitor data is sent. Nothing is sent if Shopify is not configured. Governed by Shopify’s Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

  24. Your own outbound webhook URLs — optional. Only active if you add one or more webhook endpoints in VaultFeed → Webhooks. When an event you selected fires (feed refreshed, feed error, post approved/rejected), a JSON payload is POSTed to the URL(s) you entered: the event name, the feed ID, and for refresh events each post’s platform ID, type, source, caption text (first 280 characters), permalink, and publish date. Requests are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using your webhook secret. The destination is whatever server you specify, so its terms and privacy policy are those of the service you choose; no data goes anywhere unless you add a URL.

  25. Social platform media CDNs (for example scontent.cdninstagram.com, pbs.twimg.com, i.ytimg.com — the exact hosts depend on the platforms you connect) — the images, thumbnails and videos inside your feeds are served from the platform’s own CDN, so a visitor’s browser requests them directly from that platform while viewing the feed, exactly as an ordinary embedded post would. The URLs come from the platform API response; VaultFeed does not rehost them. The platform’s terms and privacy policy are the ones listed for that platform above. If you would rather your visitors never contact those CDNs, switch on the built-in image proxy — wp option update vaultfeed_image_proxy_enabled 1 — and your own server fetches and caches the images instead.

  26. YouTube embedded player (www.youtube-nocookie.com) — only when a visitor clicks a YouTube video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads YouTube’s player directly, so YouTube receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. YouTube Terms, Google Privacy Policy.

  27. Vimeo embedded player (player.vimeo.com) — only when a visitor clicks a Vimeo video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads Vimeo’s player directly, so Vimeo receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. Vimeo Terms, Vimeo Privacy Policy.

  28. TikTok embedded player (www.tiktok.com) — only when a visitor clicks a TikTok video; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads TikTok’s player directly, so TikTok receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address and the video ID, and may set cookies. TikTok Terms, TikTok Privacy Policy.

  29. Twitch embedded player (player.twitch.tv for videos, clips.twitch.tv for clips) — only when a visitor clicks a Twitch video or clip; nothing loads before the click. The visitor’s browser then loads Twitch’s player directly, so Twitch receives the visitor’s IP address, browser details, your page address (your site’s host name is passed as the parent setting Twitch requires) and the video or clip ID, and may set cookies. Twitch Terms, Twitch Privacy Policy.

  30. WordPress.org update API — standard WordPress plugin update check behaviour. No VaultFeed-specific data is transmitted beyond the plugin slug and current version.

Third-party libraries

VaultFeed’s own scripts, styles and fonts are all bundled with the plugin — none are loaded from an external server or CDN. (The post images and videos inside your feeds are a separate matter: those are served from the social platforms’ CDNs, as described in item 25 of “External services” above.)

  • SortableJS 1.15.7 (MIT licence) — drag-to-reorder on the admin Moderation screen. Bundled at assets/js/vendor/sortable.min.js with the unminified source alongside at assets/js/vendor/sortable.js and the upstream licence at assets/js/vendor/sortable-LICENSE.txt. Source: github.com/SortableJS/Sortable.
  • All other minified files in assets/js/*.min.js and assets/css/*.min.css are built from the human-readable .js / .css files of the same name that ship next to them.

upgrade_notice.0.9.4: Wizard fixes, all ten post styles and eleven layouts everywhere, readable text in dark mode, in classic-theme sidebars and on tinted pages, the classic widget and right-to-left sites. A feed refreshes at the interval it shows, and X accounts that renew themselves no longer ask for a reconnect.
upgrade_notice.0.9.3: Feeds on quiet pages now refresh on schedule, and the stale-feed email is sent once per problem and says why. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.0.9.2: Fixes a feed's Custom CSS not appearing on the page and the highlight hero leaving an empty strip on wide pages. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.0.9.1: YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and Twitch videos now play in the lightbox; fixes the YouTube reconnect warning and the last sync time.
upgrade_notice.0.9.0: Bug-fix release: live preview, aggregate members, stored filters, widget feeds, aggregate RSS caching, block-editor feed names and a cleaner upload reader. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.0.8.9: Security and bug-fix release: closes cached-render and RSS/REST cache leaks of restricted feeds and picker exposure, and the wizard no longer resets filter or display settings when you edit a feed. No database changes.
upgrade_notice.0.8.5: Bug-fix release: aggregated feeds save again, exported feeds import again (old export files included), and the wizard no longer logs PHP deprecation notices. No database changes.

upgrade_notice.0.8.1: Security and compliance release. Database tables are renamed automatically (vf_* to vaultfeed_*) with no data loss. If your site is behind Cloudflare or a reverse proxy, set VaultFeed → Settings → Reverse Proxy / CDN after updating.
